draft.title: Structure of a persuasive essay
card: Introduction
It states the writer's position on the topic. It may also give a short preview of the arguments to come.
Body paragraphs
Each one makes a single argument. It opens with a topic sentence that names the argument, then backs it up with evidence.
Evidence
Evidence is a fact, a statistic, an expert's view or an example that supports the argument. It shows the reader the argument is sound.
Conclusion
It restates the position in fresh words and sums up the case. It does not bring in a new argument.
draft.remember: State the position, prove it one argument at a time, then restate it.

a.q: Which sentence would work best as the start of a body paragraph in an essay arguing that schools should start later?
opts: Later starts help teenagers because they need more sleep
In conclusion, schools should start later in the morning
Many students walk to school and some catch a bus
I will now explain why I like sleeping in on weekdays
a.why: A body paragraph opens with a topic sentence that names one argument, here sleep. The conclusion-style sentence is tempting, but it restates the position and belongs at the end of the essay.
a.clue: A body paragraph begins by naming its one argument.

b.q: Jai's essay argues that his town needs a skate park. His conclusion says skating is cheap and also adds a new argument about tourism. What is the problem with this conclusion?
opts: It adds a new argument instead of restating the position
It states his position again in different words
It sums up the case that he made in the essay
It ends the essay with a clear final sentence
b.why: A conclusion restates the position and sums up the case. Bringing in a new argument about tourism means it has no evidence and was not developed in a body paragraph. Restating the position in new words is correct, so that is not the fault.
b.clue: Ask whether the tourism point was proved in a body paragraph.

a.best: Later starts help teenagers because they need more sleep

b.best: It adds a new argument instead of restating the position

problems.detail: The stem already says the conclusion 'adds a new argument about tourism', and the right option repeats that exact phrase. A student can match the wording without knowing what a conclusion should do.
The right option is clearly the longest and the only one that names a fault ('instead of...'). The other three describe what a good conclusion does, so the answer stands out.

a.q: Which sentence would work best as the start of a body paragraph in an essay arguing that schools should start later?
opts: Later starts help teenagers because they need more sleep
In conclusion, schools should start later in the morning
Many students walk to school and some catch a bus
I will now explain why I like sleeping in on weekdays
a.why: A body paragraph opens with a topic sentence that names one argument, here sleep. The conclusion-style sentence is tempting, but it restates the position and belongs at the end of the essay.
a.clue: A body paragraph begins by naming its one argument.

b.q: Jai's essay argues that his town needs a skate park. His body paragraphs are about cost and safety. His conclusion restates his position, then says a skate park would bring tourists to town. What is wrong with this conclusion?
opts: It brings in a point the body did not prove
It restates the position from the introduction
It sums up the case made in the body paragraphs
It uses fresh words to state his position again
b.why: Tourism was never argued or backed with evidence in a body paragraph, so it is a new argument, which a conclusion should not include. Restating the position from the introduction is tempting to pick, but that is exactly what a conclusion is meant to do.
b.clue: Check which body paragraphs Jai actually wrote.
